When I moved back from my university address, I contacted the practice to register, and they reassured me that my records would automatically be transferred from my university GP. Two and a half months later, they still had no record of me.

During this time, I was stuck in an email back-and-forth between the two practices. Victoria Medical Centre repeatedly told me to contact my old GP to release my files, while my university GP made it clear that it is standard practice for the new GP to request the records themselves. My emails to Victoria Medical Centre eventually went unanswered, so I had to start calling multiple times—only to be told again to “wait” for my old GP to send them.

I then attended an appointment for a test I’d recently had, only for the doctor to tell me they had no access to any of my medical history, making it difficult to interpret my results. This wasted both my time and theirs.

When I called both GP practices later that day, they each confirmed—again—that it is the responsibility of the new GP (Victoria Medical Centre) to request my records. After months of emails, calls, confusion, and even GP visits, Victoria Medical Centre finally sent the request, yet still claimed I wasn’t registered with them—despite having carried out a test for me just two weeks prior.

I honestly don’t understand how the Care Quality Commission has given this practice such high ratings when the quality of administrative support is so poor.
